title: God Understands Evil
hook: Would God burn forever a child who was raised from birth to hate?
tldr: No child is born a hater. A boy like Ahmed, indoctrinated from birth, never had a real chance. Human freedom is always heavily conditioned, and dark spiritual forces wound and steer us. So God's goal is to destroy sin, not sinners: heal the infection, not kill the patient, until all are restored.
big_idea: God destroys the infection of evil, not the wounded patient.

points.title: No child is born a hater
points.text: Only trauma and indoctrination in hatred twist innocent hearts into instruments of violence. Child soldiers were never given a chance like a pastor's kid in Texas.

points.title: We don't know what we don't know
points.text: No human grasps all truth. We are formed unconsciously by inherited narratives; our freedom is real but never absolute, always heavily conditioned.

points.title: God is not binary
points.text: Divine justice is not bliss versus torment. Refining fire and lost rewards are real, but not endless torment, and even violent death is temporary if all are restored.

points.title: We wrestle against spiritual powers
points.text: Dark forces lie behind terrorists and murderers like puppeteers, and Satan even attacks the church's doctrines, explaining grotesque theologies unlike God's character.

points.title: A universal war needs universal redemption
points.text: Since the conflict is spiritual and universal, salvation must be universal too, leaving the dark powers with nothing and not one soul behind.

sections.h: A boy named Ahmed: infancy to age three
sections.summary: No baby longs to murder; trauma and indoctrination twist innocent hearts. Ahmed, born in Gaza, heard from loudspeakers words like Shahid, Jihad, evil Zionists and martyrdom, and that Allah is a God of revenge. At three he was praised for chanting hateful phrases he did not understand; his uncle gave him a toy gun, calling him Allah's lion against the Jews who would bring his family honor.

His picture books told of boys dying to fight Jews, pictured as one cursed, dehumanized people with horns: a Jew justly punished for betraying the Prophet, a teenager lifted to paradise for throwing a stone at a Jew. He learned paradise was closest to the brave, bravery meant resistance, resistance meant bloodshed. At five, an imam quoting Quran fragments taught that fighting Jews was divine will: "To fight is to believe."

At seven Ahmed played "ambush" against cardboard Jews and practiced knife grips, praised by a brother with martyr photos on his wall; at dinners a Jerusalem bakery bomber was honored as being in paradise. He never learned Hebrew, met Jewish children or heard stories of peace or shared pain. By thirteen, driven by sexual desire, he was told he would receive 72 virgins for dying in violence against Jews and Christians.

At fifteen his play had become preparation and he no longer smiled. A militant recruiter at the mosque praised him as pure and ready to make Allah proud. The boy with a toy gun now held a real one, seeing only black and white: us and them. He was promised instant paradise. He never knew the faces he hated; he did not know better.

This may sound like fiction to "enlightened" Western ears, but it is everyday reality in parts of the Middle East and Africa, where Hamas, Hezbollah, ISIS, Boko Haram and Islamic Jihad have often used brainwashed children as soldiers. Child soldiering is evil at its worst; these children were never truly given a chance, certainly not like a pastor's kid born into a Christian family in Texas.

sections.h: We don't realize what we don't know
sections.summary: Not being all-knowing, the human mind cannot grasp all truth. From birth we are formed, often unconsciously, by inherited narratives. We choose freely, but never absolutely; our freedom is heavily conditioned. Here God's understanding and mercy come in. Young terrorists are not in for a garden of roses, but God is not binary: divine justice is not a simple equation of bliss versus torment.

Being refined and purified by fire is hardly pleasant, but losing reward or facing consequences need not mean endless hellfire, as some Christian and Islamic traditions claim. If all will ultimately be restored, even tragic, violent deaths are not the final word: everyone will be resurrected and restored, making the worst death temporary. If God's grace is not bigger than ours, it is not divine grace.

sections.h: We wrestle not against flesh and blood
sections.summary: Beyond culture, spiritual forces shape fragile, impressionable humans. Ephesians 6:12 says our struggle is against principalities, powers and spiritual wickedness in high places. Dark forces lurk behind every terrorist and murderer, pulling strings like marionettes, figuratively or perhaps literally through possession. Satan also attacks the church: its beliefs, doctrines, Bible translations, commentaries and teachings, explaining conflicting theologies so grotesquely unlike God that only spiritual deception could produce them.

All creation is in a spiritual battle most people do not even notice. A spiritual, universal struggle demands universal salvation, as far-reaching as the battle and not limited by human awareness. If the main conflict is with powers far stronger than us, humans are image-bearers under assault, not inherently evil. God's task is to eradicate sin, not sinners: like healing a disease, destroying the infection, not killing the patient. Christ's full victory leaves evil with nothing.

sections.h: Conclusion: the world is being saved
sections.summary: God wants "all people to be saved" (1 Timothy 2:4), showing His power to defeat the true enemies, sin and evil, not the people they influence. As evil and death do not discriminate, neither does salvation. Evil is deeper than individuals and salvation wider than our categories. Justice ends in healing and restoration; sin is judged and undone, but the image-bearer is never discarded. The world is not being thrown away; it is being saved.

mythfact.myth: Terrorists are simply evil people who freely chose hatred.
mythfact.fact: No child is born a hater. Children like Ahmed are indoctrinated from birth and never given a real chance.

mythfact.myth: Divine justice is a simple choice between bliss and torment.
mythfact.fact: God is not binary. Refining fire and lost rewards are real consequences, but they need not mean endless torment.
God's task is to eradicate sin itself, like destroying an infection rather than killing the patient.
